brief.user: Dr. Ifeoma Daniels, coordinator of the service-learning program at an urban public university. She places students from six courses each semester and knows most partner organizations personally.

Ifeoma is working through the 34 partner sites spread across the city, looking at where they sit relative to campus, bus and light-rail lines, and the neighborhoods students live in. brief.data: 34 partner sites, each with an address, neighborhood, organization type (food pantry, tutoring, refugee resettlement, legal clinic, senior center, community garden), spring capacity (2–12 students), available time slots, and transit access (nearest stop, routes, minutes from campus). prompt:
I need the front end for Commonplace Placements. A university service-learning office's tool for matching students to community nonprofit partner sites across the city, based on where the sites are and how students can get there.

Who's using it: Dr. Ifeoma Daniels, coordinator of the service-learning program at an urban public university. She places students from six courses each semester and knows most partner organizations personally.

What they're doing right now: Spring semester placements are due to faculty on Friday. Ifeoma is working through the 34 partner sites spread across the city, looking at where they sit relative to campus, bus and light-rail lines, and the neighborhoods students live in. Most students don't have cars, and a site more than 45 minutes away by transit tends to lose volunteers mid-term. She needs to pick sites for the 27 students still unplaced, especially the 9 who need weekday-evening slots.

What's in the system at this point: 34 partner sites, each with an address, neighborhood, organization type (food pantry, tutoring, refugee resettlement, legal clinic, senior center, community garden), spring capacity (2–12 students), available time slots, and transit access (nearest stop, routes, minutes from campus). Examples: Eastside Community Pantry (capacity 8, 5 filled, 22 min on Route 7), Harbor Literacy Project (capacity 6, 6 filled), Northgate Refugee Welcome Center (capacity 10, 3 filled, 51 min with a transfer), Cedar Street Senior Center (evenings, capacity 4). 118 students placed so far, 27 unplaced. Each unplaced student has a course (e.g., SOC 140, PUBH 101), home neighborhood, transit mode, and preferred slots. Light-rail Blue Line extension opened Sept 2026, adding 4 stations.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
